request.spec:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now have a status, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What it does:**
- **Rules:** a new claim starts as DRAFT. DRAFT can go to OPEN, OPEN to SETTLED, and DRAFT or OPEN to VOID. SETTLED and VOID claims can't change. The server checks every change, and a refused one saves nothing and writes no audit line.
- **Audit:** each change writes `CLAIM_OPENED`, `CLAIM_SETTLED` or `CLAIM_VOIDED`, followed by `sheet= by= person= amount= date=`.
- **On screen:** each claim row shows its status and has Open, Settle and Void buttons. All three are always shown. Pressing one that isn't allowed shows an error on that claim, and the error clears on the claim's next action.
- **Totals:** only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward the person's claimed amount, their due-total and the sheet's claimed and due totals. Each claim still shows its own due, even when it's a draft or voided, because the test expects that.

**Changes:**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V7__claim_status.sql`, adds a `status` column that defaults to `DRAFT`.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/status`, takes `{status, by}`. It's built from new classes `ClaimStatus`, `ValidateClaimStatus`, `ApplyClaimStatus` and `RecordClaimStatus`. The claim's status is also stored, loaded and returned in the claim data.
- **Front end:** a new `features/claims/status.slot.tsx` adds the status and buttons to the claim row. A `counts()` helper in `useClaims.ts` decides which claims go into the totals, used both there and in `rates.slot.tsx`.

The request didn't say whether a SETTLED or VOID claim can still be edited, so I left editing unchanged: any claim can still be edited whatever its status.
